clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2: the PoolManager inputs that a speculative result could get wrong (own native balance, token balance, transient storage, hook code, SSTORE originals).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read src/types/Currency.sol:90-92: balanceOfSelf returns address(this).balance only for address zero. Its callers are sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), which takes the else branch only for a nonzero currency, and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), which calls it only when the synced currency is nonzero and otherwise uses msg.value. So production code never observes its own native balance. Native take uses CALL with value (src/types/Currency.sol:45-49) and reverts on failure. In reth, a value send records an AtLeast bound and compare refuses a current balance below it (reuse.rs 386-389). In Monad, record_balance_constraint_for_debit sets a minimum or an exact balance (state.cpp 712 onward). A token balance is token storage, which both read sets compare exactly. The item holds.

clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched monad v0.16.7 category/execution/ethereum/state3/state.cpp and evmc_host.cpp. EvmcHostBase::get_balance calls State::get_balance (evmc_host.cpp lines 82-88), which sets validate_exact_balance on the original account state (state.cpp lines 233-241). try_fix_account_mismatch (state.cpp lines 650-710) refuses when either side is dead, when code hash, incarnation or nonce differ, when relaxed validation is off, when the balance was read exactly, or when the actual balance is below the recorded minimum, and then shifts the current balance by the difference. This matches the cleared item. I did not refetch block_state.cpp for can_merge and rely on the cycle 24 copy for that part. Because the PoolManager never reads its own native balance (previous check), the relaxed rule can only shift a balance that no PoolManager decision depends on.
